data.current_summary: Risk verdict, network and location for one IP address
data.current_description:
Free without a key (per-client-IP allowance) or with a key (your own allowance). Never cache the verdict across decisions: `computed_at` says when it was computed and `risk.score` decays with the age of the evidence. The `risk` object has the same shape as on `/pulse/v1/ip/{ip}` (`score` / `level` / `signals`), rendered by the same function: this endpoint just omits the professional extras `evidence[]`, `share_tier` and `resource_pools`, and adds one field Pulse does not have — `degraded`, a basic-tier-only marker that appears (and is true) only when one evidence source was unavailable and the verdict was computed without it.

The hit signals are carried by `risk.signals` alone, and an address that hit nothing omits that key entirely.
data.summary_suggestion: Lookup IP risk verdict with geolocation and network data
data.description_suggestion: Returns a risk verdict for the given IP address, including proxy/VPN/datacenter detection, geolocation (city-level globally, district-level in China), and network information. The `risk` object contains `score`, `level`, and `signals` indicating detected threats. Access is free without authentication (1000 lookups/day per client IP, 60/minute) or with an API key for higher quotas. Critical: do not cache verdicts—`computed_at` indicates when the verdict was computed and `risk.score` reflects evidence freshness. The `degraded` field (true only when an evidence source was unavailable) signals incomplete verdicts. Addresses with no detected signals omit the `risk.signals` key entirely.

data.current_summary: Same verdict with per-evidence detail (professional tier)
data.current_description: Same engine, the same score and the same `risk` object as `/v1/ip/{ip}` (both render `score` / `level` / `signals` with the same function), plus per-evidence detail, sharing tier and resource pools. `risk.signals` lists only the signals that fired, sorted alphabetically; an address that hit nothing omits that key. Requires a key on the professional data tier; without it the API answers HTTP 403 `professional_required`. `?at=` returns the verdict as it stood at a past moment (history window per contract) and the response has exactly the same fields and shape as a live one; only `computed_at` changes meaning, while `risk.signals`, `network` and `geo` stay current. The risk labels ride on the evidence rows as `evidence[].risk_type` (the ones that are also signals come back again in `risk.signals`), and every row of `evidence[]` carries exactly five keys: `risk_type`, `freshness` and `obs_days` always, plus `captured_at` and `age_min` when they have a value. There is no degraded flag in the body — that marker is basic-tier-only and sits on `/v1/ip/{ip}`: here a verdict computed with one evidence source missing is signalled by the `X-Pulse-Degraded: 1` response header.
data.summary_suggestion: Lookup IP risk with detailed evidence and historical verdicts
data.description_suggestion: Returns a detailed IP risk verdict (professional tier) including the same `risk` object as `/v1/ip/{ip}` plus per-evidence breakdown in `evidence[]` array, sharing tier, and resource pools. Each evidence row contains `risk_type`, `freshness`, `obs_days`, and optionally `captured_at` and `age_min`. Requires professional-tier API key; returns HTTP 403 if not authorized. Supports historical lookups via `?at=<timestamp>` parameter to retrieve verdicts from past moments (within contract history window); historical responses have the same structure with current `risk.signals`, `network`, and `geo` data. Incomplete verdicts (missing evidence source) are signaled by the `X-Pulse-Degraded: 1` response header. `risk.signals` lists only fired signals in alphabetical order; addresses with no signals omit this key.
